column1: # source: WRITTEN FROM KNOWLEDGE, not extracted from any book or database. The base -> target pairs are the derivational and semantic relations historical linguists treat as ordinary: instrument, agent, result and place nouns from verbs; diminutives; denominal and deadjectival verbs; 'X-like' qualities; causatives. Modelled on Buck 1949 (A Dictionary of Selected Synonyms in the Principal Indo-European Languages, Chicago), Urban 2012 (Analyzability and Semantic Associations in Referring Expressions, Leiden; cross-linguistic motivation patterns of 160 meanings), Koch 2008 (lexical motivation), Pokorny 1959 / LIV2 2001 (PIE root families such as *bher- 'carry'), Haspelmath & Tadmor 2009 (WOLD, the IDS semantic fields) and Heine & Kuteva 2002 (the function-word rows).

# version: hand-authored 2026-11-04 (procedural-language lane, word families and derivation round); extended 2026-11-07 (round 5, the WOLD extension of concepts.tsv: agents, instruments, causatives and kin-term shifts for the new meanings)
# licence: original text for this repository (no third-party data copied); cite the works above when using it.

# CLICS3: at load time lexicon.py joins each pair with data/clics_edges.tsv; a pair CLICS3 also attests as a colexification in >= 3 families (BLOOD/RED, MOUNTAIN/HILL, TREE/FOREST ...) gets its family count added to the weight (a motivated pair is often colexified too).

# columns: relation = the affix meaning (agent 'one who', thing 'instrument / result / object', place 'place of', little 'small / young / diminutive', like 'X-like, having X', do 'make / do X, verb from a noun or quality', cause 'make (someone) V'), or reinforce (a function word renewed by compounding with the base: Latin ecce + iste > French ce 'this'; the Jespersen cycle, Old English na-wiht 'no thing' > not), or repair (the same, used only to renew a pronoun, numeral or deictic cell that sound change merged with another cell of its paradigm: lexicon.core_repair; Spanish nosotros, French il); base and target = concept ids of planet/language/lexicon.py; weight = typicality 1 (attested, uncommon) .. 3 (common across families); example = one or two real cases (romanized) or the bare motivation.

# A target may sit on several rows; derivation picks among the rows whose base the lexicon has. Only these pairs derive (plus two renewals in lexicon.py: the expressive diminutive, lexicon.RENEW_LITTLE, a noun or quality replaced by its own diminutive: Latin auricula > French oreille 'ear', avicellus > oiseau 'bird', soliculus > soleil 'sun', vetulus > vieux 'old', novellus > nouveau 'new'; and the frequentative or preverb renewal of verbs, lexicon.RENEW_INTENS: Latin canere > cantare 'sing', iacere > iactare 'throw', edere > comedere > Spanish comer 'eat').
# Content words from function words are kept to three rows of weight 1 (STRANGER < OTHER / FAR is a quality); function words derive among themselves (here < this + place).

# shift rows (2026-11-04, compounds and shifts round): base > target = a semantic shift (the target concept takes the base's word) attested across families although the two concepts sit in different semantic fields (lexicon.shift_word otherwise allows a shift only along a CLICS3 colexification of >= 6 families, >= 10 for the core vocabulary, inside one concepts.tsv / CLICS3 semantic field and part of speech). Polysemies listed both ways where both directions are attested; sources: Buck 1949, Wilkins 1996 (Natural tendencies of semantic change and the search for cognates, in Durie & Ross eds., The Comparative Method Reviewed), Sweetser 1990 (From Etymology to Pragmatics: SEE > KNOW, HEAR > KNOW), Heine & Kuteva 2002 (World Lexicon of Grammaticalization: the content > function word rows, BELLY > IN, WITH > AND, ONE > SOME), Urban 2012, CLICS3 family counts. A pathway may cross parts of speech (grammaticalization); other shifts may not.
